clue.text: Great guy from East needs minute inside shops

indicators.note: in an across entry, reading from the east means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with the digit as the letter I

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another means a letter is slotted into the middle of a longer string

parts.note: a guy is a rope that holds a tent or mast steady
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Some splendid fellow from the East needs a minute inside the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great guy' reads as an admiring phrase, but it is two words: A1 for great and ROPE for guy. Reverse them to get EPORIA, then put M after the first letter: EMPORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large store or trading place selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: Hard to follow The King's Speech

indicators.note: something that follows comes after, so this letter is placed at the end of the other piece

parts.note: Elvis Presley is known as the King of rock and roll
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The film The King's Speech is said to be difficult to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title tempts you to read the clue whole, but The King is Elvis rather than George VI, and H follows him to give ELVISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvish is the invented language of the elves in Tolkien, a form of speech in that fictional world.

clue.text: Agent X after stuff on radio

indicators.note: coming after places this piece at the end, behind the other one
radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to stuff is to fill, which sounds like the name Phil
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' as in two by four

explanation.surface: A secret agent called X is chasing material broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby was a British intelligence officer who spied for the Soviet Union; he links this puzzle's theme, The Third Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Philby was a real double agent, so his surname stands for one particular example of a spy.

clue.text: Rotten Row recreated outside small place like Margate?

indicators.note: lying outside means wrapping around, so the longer string goes round the short one
something recreated is made again from scratch, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the nine letters of the name, to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Rotten Row, the riding track in Hyde Park, is being rebuilt outside some small seaside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a bridleway in London's Hyde Park, and its name supplies all nine letters to rearrange. Margate is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a classic English seaside holiday destination, an example of a town people visit for leisure; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Snake one caught in savoury jelly

parts.note: an asp is a small venomous snake
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A snake has got itself stuck in a savoury jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught in' looks like a container instruction, but 'caught' is C and 'in' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a clear jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes such as eggs or ham.

clue.text: Punk's green hair pushed back

indicators.note: something pushed back goes in the opposite direction, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: green means inexperienced, and a naif is an innocent
fur is an animal's hair

explanation.surface: A punk rocker's dyed green hair has been slicked back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. 'Green hair' looks like a punk hairdo, but it is two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: A punk, in its older sense, is a young thug or hoodlum, which is what a ruffian is.

clue.text: Rook — different meat in northern town

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook
other means different
ham is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: A rook bird is seen eating a different kind of meat in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook is a chess piece here, not a bird: R in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotherham is an industrial town in South Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Skin flick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thin layer covering a surface
second meaning: a movie, in slang

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest an adult movie, but each is a separate meaning of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is both a thin coating layer on a surface and, informally, a motion picture shown in cinemas.

clue.text: Is it pub-o'clock before you know it?

parts.note: surface reading: asking whether it is time to head for a drink
setter's reading: a pub is an inn, and an hour on the clock is a time, so an inn's time run together sounds like the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly asks whether drinking time has arrived already.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as INN O' TIME and it becomes 'pub o'clock', the hour for the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly, so soon that something happens almost without your noticing.

clue.text: Irritating being short of Liberal dons

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so one piece wears the other round a letter

parts.note: being short of something is needing it
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: University dons who lack liberal views are annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers, but it is the verb: NEEDING puts on L.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling someone is provoking or annoying them with persistent jibes, so it is a near synonym.

clue.text: English invested in wine initially stored in vessels

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: vin is French for wine, familiar from vin rouge
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: English money has been put into wine kept in barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' looks like the barrels holding the wine, but here it means blood vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Veins are blood vessels that carry blood back to the heart, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Pamper uncle with a ruptured spleen

parts.note: to pet is to pamper or fuss over

indicators.note: something ruptured is burst apart, so these letters are broken and reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look after your uncle, who has a ruptured spleen.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruptured spleen sounds medical, but the spleen is the definition: the old sense of bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means ill temper or peevish anger, the organ having been thought the seat of moods, so it matches sulky irritability.

clue.text: Withdrawn journalist clutching pamphlet

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip tightly, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a sub-ed is a subeditor, a newspaper journalist who checks copy
a tract is a short pamphlet, usually religious or political

explanation.surface: A shy, reserved reporter holds tight to a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' suggests a shy person, but here it means taken away. SUB-ED is a crossword staple for a subeditor.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take away or deduct, as money is withdrawn from an account, so the past participles match.

clue.text: And others towards the end returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back where it came from, so the letters travel backwards

parts.note: late means near the end of a period

explanation.surface: Other people came back towards the end.
explanation.walkthrough: ET AL is short for the Latin et alii, used after a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation is used in citations to mean that further people, beyond those named, are included.

clue.text: Hairstyle associated with old school member?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short-at-front, long-at-back haircut that has gone grey with age
second meaning: a fish, since fish swim in schools

explanation.surface: A haircut linked with a former pupil of some old school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old school' looks like a phrase, but 'old' ends the first meaning and 'school' means a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey mullet is a common coastal fish that swims in shoals, and a mullet worn by an older person would be grey.

clue.text: Male in each community coming out

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so a letter is placed within a short word

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
M is the abbreviation for male
a nation is a community of people

explanation.surface: Gay men in every community are announcing their sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' suggests revealing one's sexuality, but here it means flowing out of a source.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something issuing or flowing from a source, like light or gas, so it is the act of coming out.

clue.text: Like some speeches in part Sweeney's source yelled about?

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the name

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
PT is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: Sweeney Todd's lines in the play are shouted out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a theatrical role, which suits the speeches, but it is only its abbreviation; 'Sweeney's source' is the first letter of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A scripted speech is written out in advance rather than improvised, as many political addresses are.

clue.text: Flexible girl taking walk outside

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps around it, so the longer word encloses the shorter

parts.note: to amble is to walk slowly
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A supple, sporty girl is going for a walk outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' in crosswords is usually a short name to be guessed; this one is a stock three-letter name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is willing to go along with things and open to persuasion, which is a figurative kind of flexibility.

clue.text: Old PM with Larry say devouring old gull hearts regardless

indicators.note: to devour is to swallow whole, so one piece takes others inside it

parts.note: Larry is the cat at 10 Downing Street, the UK prime minister's home
O is the abbreviation for old
a mew is a seagull
H is the abbreviation for hearts, the card suit
Theresa May was a recent UK prime minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister and the Downing Street cat watch it eat an old seagull's heart regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Larry as an example of his kind of animal. The prime minister is named first in the clue but goes at the end of the answer, since 'with' only joins pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means whatever happens, so it says one will go ahead regardless of the outcome.

clue.text: Emerald Isle's ultimate writer

parts.note: emerald is a shade of green

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ireland, the Emerald Isle, produced the greatest writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emerald Isle' reads as Ireland, but Emerald is a colour and Isle gives only its last letter. Graham Greene wrote the script for The Third Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist and screenwriter, so his surname is an example of an author.

clue.text: Article One's written about singular subject

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: about means turned round, so these letters are written the other way

parts.note: one is I, and the apostrophe-S turns that into I'S
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about one particular topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition or theme put forward for discussion, so it is the topic or subject of an argument.

clue.text: Scandinavians not loud boozers

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Finns are people from Finland, counted as Scandinavians
F is forte, the musical instruction for loud

explanation.surface: People from Scandinavia who are not rowdy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozers' looks like heavy drinkers, but in British slang a boozer is a pub. Remove F from FINNS.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a boozer is a pub, and an inn is a pub too, so the plurals are synonyms.

clue.text: Review ultra-harsh for final performance

indicators.note: to review is to look at something again and revise it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the ten letters, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A critic writes a scathing notice of an actor's farewell show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' looks like a theatre critic's notice, which fits the performance, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A last hurrah is a final effort or appearance before retirement, a farewell showing at the end of a career.

clue.text: Flower Romeo dropped into Spanish wine

indicators.note: something dropped into a thing ends up inside it, so a letter goes within a word

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, historically from Alicante
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo drops a flower into a glass of Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; it is something that flows, a river. The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is often a river, something that flows, and the Trent is one of England's longest rivers.

clue.text: Ancient arrow point bloodied all around

indicators.note: something all around another surrounds it, so one word encloses a letter

parts.note: something bloodied is red
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An old arrowhead covered in blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrow point' reads as an arrowhead, but 'point' belongs to the wordplay as a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Early arrows were made from reed stems, so in poetic or archaic usage reed means an arrow shaft.

clue.text: Drink to Scots having arrived unexpectedly

indicators.note: having means holding, so one word keeps another inside it

parts.note: tae is the Scottish form of to
to blow in is to turn up without warning

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to the Scots, who turned up out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink to' looks like a toast, but 'Drink' alone is the definition and 'to Scots' is the Scottish TAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Table wine is ordinary wine served with meals, so it is a type of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Elland Road team tops league did you say?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: a side that tops a table is in front of the rest

explanation.surface: A football fan asks whether their club is top of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Elland Road is the stadium of Leeds United, an English football club usually called simply Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds United play their home matches at Elland Road, so the club is the side based there.

clue.text: Prepare without finishing study in China

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to dress food or a wound is to prepare it
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Get ready to go and study in China without finishing the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden china is fine porcelain made near the German city, so the name stands for that type of tableware.

clue.text: Teetotaller in bank finally gets giggles

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within a word

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A non-drinker sitting on a riverbank ends up having a fit of the giggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a river or money, but it is a row, TIER, which holds TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a short nervous or suppressed laugh, so as a verb it means much the same as giggles.
